credential: Free Open University Statement of Participation and digital badge after completion and required quizzes; course also states 24 CPD points
academic_credits: No academic credit for the OpenLearn route
scope_notes: Eight-week, approximately 24-hour intermediate course on effective online teaching, covering learner preparation, synchronous/asynchronous design, learning technologies, inclusion, accessibility, wellbeing, collaboration, online assessment and professional practice.
prerequisites: No formal prerequisites; designed for educators, trainers, support staff and education leaders moving teaching partly or fully online
required_resources: Modern browser; a free OpenLearn account is needed for progress tracking, quizzes, badge and Statement of Participation; downloadable offline formats are available

component_evidence.pedagogy: The course is explicitly designed around the experience of online learners and educators, combining research, teacher reflections, practical decisions and weekly progression rather than presenting a catalogue of digital tools.
component_evidence.depth: Eight weeks and roughly 24 hours provide substantial professional-development depth across pedagogy, learner support, technology selection, inclusion, assessment and changing educator practice.
component_evidence.practice: Weekly quizzes, activities, reflection, planning and an end-of-course badge quiz require learners to apply decisions to their own teaching context, although no externally reviewed classroom capstone is documented.
component_evidence.materials: OpenLearn provides structured weekly content, videos, research references, quizzes, activities and unusually broad downloadable formats including PDF, EPUB, HTML and IMS Common Cartridge.
component_evidence.currency: The course was last formally updated in October 2022. Core online-teaching principles remain current, but named digital platforms and parts of the technology landscape have changed since then.
component_evidence.expertise: The Open University has extensive institutional experience in online and distance education, and the course explicitly draws on its research and long-running online-teaching practice.
component_evidence.accessibility: The full course is free, self-paced, downloadable and can be started without registration; a free account unlocks assessment, progress tracking, statement and badge.

recommendation_rationale: The strongest broad teacher-development course in the current Education survivor family: substantial, evidence-informed and genuinely designed for independent practice. Its main caveat is the 2022 technology snapshot, not pedagogy.

credential: Free British Council TeachingEnglish certificate of achievement after successful completion of the self-study modules
scope_notes: Current 9–12-hour three-module English-teacher CPD course on evaluating teaching resources, adapting and selecting lesson plans for context and inclusion, and using learners' own knowledge and contributions as classroom resources.
prerequisites: Practising or developing English-language teachers; British Council TeachingEnglish courses are professional-development rather than initial teaching qualifications
required_resources: Free TeachingEnglish account and browser; workbook is free, while Facebook community and live-event participation are optional

component_evidence.pedagogy: The sequence moves from evaluating materials to adapting lesson plans and then treating learners themselves as resources, keeping every module tied to concrete classroom decisions.
component_evidence.depth: Nine to twelve hours across three focused modules provides useful CPD depth but is intentionally narrower than a full methodology course or qualification.
component_evidence.practice: Learners analyse resources, adapt plans, consider inclusion and use a workbook/action-planning layer to transfer ideas to real classes; public evidence does not show a large independently assessed capstone.
component_evidence.materials: Three self-study modules, a free workbook, TeachingEnglish resource links, optional community support and expert live-event recordings provide a strong reusable package.
component_evidence.currency: This is a new current course in the 2026–27 TeachingEnglish programme, open through March 2027, and its focus on inclusive contextual adaptation is directly relevant to present teaching practice.
component_evidence.expertise: The course sits inside the British Council TeachingEnglish professional-development framework and is supported by a specialist ELT teacher-development programme with global classroom experience.
component_evidence.accessibility: Course, workbook and certificate are free, self-paced within the active window and require only a free account; the main access limitation is the time-bounded annual course window.

recommendation_rationale: A very strong practical recommendation for English teachers who need to evaluate and adapt materials to local learners rather than simply consume ready-made lesson plans. Its focused 9–12-hour scope is the main depth limit.

credential: Free British Council TeachingEnglish certificate of achievement after successful completion of the self-study modules
scope_notes: Current 9–12-hour three-module teacher-educator course on understanding teacher learning and training, facilitating communities of practice and collaborative learning, and supporting teacher autonomy and self-directed professional development.
prerequisites: Designed for teacher educators or teachers developing teacher-educator responsibilities
required_resources: Free TeachingEnglish account and browser; free workbook included; Facebook community and live events are optional enrichment

component_evidence.pedagogy: The course progresses from planning effective teacher learning to collaborative communities of practice and then autonomous professional learning, creating a coherent teacher-educator development arc.
component_evidence.depth: Nine to twelve hours gives substantive orientation to teacher education but remains a compact CPD course rather than a full trainer-development programme.
component_evidence.practice: The workbook includes reflection, action planning and prompts to apply new ideas, and participant examples show transfer into communities of practice; formal public evidence of a major assessed project is limited.
component_evidence.materials: Self-study modules are reinforced by a 2025 workbook, action-plan/reflection sections, optional professional community and live-event resources.
component_evidence.currency: The course is active in the 2026–27 programme through March 2027 and the current workbook is dated 2025, supporting strong present relevance.
component_evidence.expertise: British Council TeachingEnglish provides specialist international teacher-development support and frames this course specifically for teacher educators and professional-learning leadership.
component_evidence.accessibility: The course, workbook and certificate are free and self-paced during the active run, with only a free account required; the annual access window is the main friction.

recommendation_rationale: A strong specialist recommendation for teachers moving into mentoring or teacher-educator roles. It adds a distinct professional-development function rather than duplicating classroom-methodology courses, but its compact duration caps depth.
